QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_27

question.text: Asha Deep Trust claims 40% decrease in child-marriage rates in participating communities (Sakhi case). Under SAS-400, the MOST rigorous MoV is:

answer.text: A phone call to the Sarpanch
Triangulation of: (i) village marriage registers, (ii) school dropout data for girls aged 14-18, (iii) Panchayat records, (iv) sub-sample household visits

explanation.text: The Logic: Child-marriage data is under-reported; single-source evidence is weak. Triangulation across village marriage register, girls' secondary-school retention, panchayat records and field visits builds defensible evidence under SAS-400. The Trap: Option A is SE-side self-report only. Option C is single-informant. Option B is benchmark, not evidence of change. Cross-Exam Context: Multi-source triangulation also in XV Research Analyst and III-A / III-C Compliance inspection-evidence. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Always pair a child-marriage indicator with a girls'-school-retention indicator — they move inversely and the pair is harder to game than either alone.
